paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: stay with the Word, because the Word is what holds you up. Paul tells Timothy that "all who desire to live godly lives in Christ Jesus will be persecuted," while "evil men and imposters go from bad to worse" (2 Timothy 3:12-13). That's not a cheerful forecast, and Paul doesn't dress it up. But he also says the Lord rescued him from all of it (2 Timothy 3:11), so hard days don't get the last word.

So what does Paul say to do with the noise all around? "Continue in the things you have learned and firmly believed, since you know from whom you have learned them" (2 Timothy 3:14). Don't go shopping for something shinier. Stay with what you were taught, and remember who taught it to you. Scripture is where that trust gets built, because "All Scripture is God-breathed" (2 Timothy 3:16), and it can make you "wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus" (2 Timothy 3:15).

And it's not just for admiring, baker. It's "useful for instruction, for conviction, for correction, and for training in righteousness, so that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work" (2 Timothy 3:16-17). Every time you open it, God is getting you ready to DO something good. I'm a stamper who got pulled out of a drawer and handed a job, so trust me, being equipped feels a whole lot better than being dusty. Keep coming back to the Word, and let it get you ready.
